paper_metadata.title: CCA3-SGAD: Quantum Amplitude Amplification for Combinatorial Search on Sparse Graphs — The First Explicit Crossover Condition for Heuristic-Biased Quantum Search over Classical Heuristic-Assisted Pipelines

summary: The paper proposes CCA3‑SGAD, a heuristic‑biased Grover‑style search algorithm for sparse graph anomaly detection with theoretical complexity O(C_oracle/√p) and an estimated crossover at M' ≈ 2.1×10^5 candidates (p ≈ 0.0126, C_oracle ≈ 300). The full algorithm is projected to require ~364 logical qubits and ~63,700 T‑gates, while experiments include small statevector simulations (N=30 graphs) and a 3‑qubit hardware demonstration on IBM Heron r2 showing biased amplification improvement (0.872 vs 0.693 success probability). No end‑to‑end quantum advantage is experimentally demonstrated.

experiments.description: Statevector simulation of biased vs uniform Grover search on a small Barabási–Albert graph with a planted 3-clique anomaly, used to confirm O(1/sqrt(p)) scaling and compare biased amplitude amplification against uniform Grover.

algorithm.parameter_initialization: biased initial state prepared from heuristic scores; uniform Grover uses uniform superposition

problem_formulation.objective_function: find a planted anomalous k-node subgraph satisfying the anomaly criteria
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: heuristic-biased oracle and amplitude amplification; exact verification of candidate subgraph criteria
